title: Adaptive weight paging and on-demand mmap probe
content:
Status: draft
Owner: Priya Menon
Context:
This doc captures an alternative approach to model weight residency and activation that emphasizes small-page probing, adaptive residency scoring, and a safe streaming path for safetensors. The goal is to reduce cold-start latency for large shards while avoiding heavy upfront IO and to make weight activation cooperative with kernel scheduling and KV cache behavior.

High-level goals:
- Minimize tail latency for first few tokens on large models (>=30B) without preloading full shard(s).
- Provide an async, verifiable streaming path for safetensors with quarantine/atomic activation.
- Make paging decisions aware of KV cache pressures and kernel co-location to avoid thrashing.
- Allow graceful hot-swap of model patches/quantized variants with minimal disruption.

Key ideas (overview):
1) Probe-on-demand mmap: instead of immediately populating large mmapped ranges when a shard is referenced, perform a lightweight read-probe of high-value pages (attention, output, first layer kernels) based on a model-architecture fingerprint. If probe hits miss, trigger prioritized async prefetch.
2) Residency score per page-range: a small moving-score that accounts for access recency, future access probability (inferred from kernel schedule), and KV-cache pressure. Eviction and prefetch priorities derive from this unified score.
3) KV cache-aware eviction: when the KV cache grows under memory pressure, adjust residency scoring to prefer keeping KV-related parameter pages resident (key/query/value projection weights) and deprioritize embedding/FFN pages if they can be streamed.
4) Safetensors streaming with quarantine: stream safetensors shards over HTTP/sidecar, verify checksum chunks on arrival, place into a quarantine area (uncommitted tmp files + memory-mapped verification), and only commit/activate atomically when all critical page ranges pass checks.
5) Cooperative kernel hinting: scheduling layer exposes which kernels (and thus weight offsets) are likely to be used in the next N tokens; the loader uses hints to prioritize page residency ahead of scheduled execution.
6) Hot-swap with staged activation: support multi-stage activation where new weight pages are downloaded to quarantine, checksummed, soft-mapped, and then an activation pointer swap commits them and signals runtime to switch kernel pointers; previous residency can be kept until safe free.

Components and responsibilities:
- Probe Loader (component):
  - Receives model manifest + architecture fingerprint (layer layout, offloadable ranges).
  - Maintains a small static list of "high-value" page-ranges for each model family (e.g., first projection layers, lm_head).
  - On first reference, performs single-page reads (O(1) small reads) to check whether pages are resident or swapped out and triggers async prefetch of additional ranges if read misses exceed threshold.
  - Exposes metrics: probe_hit_rate, probe_latency, prefetch_trigger_count.

- Residency Scorer:
  - Tracks page-range recency (LRU-ish), kernel-hint weight, and KV-cache utility.
  - Score = alpha*recency + beta*kernel_hint + gamma*kv_utility - delta*io_cost_estimate (weights tuned).
  - Periodic normalization to avoid runaway growth; supports forced-decay windows during GC or model swap.

- Safetensors Streamer & Quarantine:
  - Pull shards in chunked mode (aligned to page size).
  - Verify per-chunk checksum and maintain an index of verified chunks.
  - Write verified chunks to a quarantine file under tmp/safestream/<job-id>/<shard>.part, create a mmapped view to allow kernel-safe reading before activation.
  - Activation step writes a lightweight manifest update and flips an atomic pointer used by weight-resolver. Old mapping remains read-only until GC.
  - If verification fails, mark chunk bad, attempt retried fetch or fall back to alternative model variant.

- Kernel Scheduler integration:
  - Scheduler provides "kernel hint" API: give next-kernel-lists for each executor (window size N=2–8). Hints map to parameter offsets.
  - Loader prioritizes residency for offsets in hints.
  - If a required offset is not yet resident at exec time, scheduler can choose to: 1) wait for prioritized async prefetch with a short spin; 2) fallback to a compatible quantized/CPU kernel; 3) spill execution to a less-loaded replica.

- KV cache-aware policies:
  - Monitor KV cache hit/life metrics; when KV cache pressure high, raise the kv_utility term for projection weights so they remain resident.
  - For models with large context windows where KV dominates working set, provide a config switch to pin KV-related parameter pages until soft pressure threshold reached.

Activation & Hot-swap protocol (staged):
1) Stage: download to quarantine, per-chunk verify.
2) Warm: mmapped verified chunks to allow reads from new mapping in parallel with old mapping (read-only). Residency scoring starts incorporating new mapping reads.
3) Commit: atomic manifest pointer swap (e.g., via update to a small file and fsync), notify all executors to resolve new manifest.
4) Drain: existing in-flight requests finish against old mapping; new requests use new mapping.
5) GC: once no references remain, unmap old and free files.

Graceful fallback strategies:
- If quarantine verification stalls, runtime falls back to a pinned, older quantized variant (if available) to preserve latency SLOs.
- If prefetch bandwidth saturated, we prioritize kernel-hinted ranges and deprioritize background prefetch for low-score pages.

Metrics to collect (minimum):
- probe_hit_rate, probe_miss_latency
- chunk_verify_rate, chunk_verify_errors
- prefetch_bytes/sec, prefetch_failures
- page_fault-induced-execution-pauses, average_pause_ms
- residency_score_distribution, eviction_count_by_category (kv, ffn, embedding)
- hot_swap_commit_latency, activation_failures

Testing & experiments plan:
- Microbenchmarks: measure probe cost vs immediate mmap for 4 models (7B/13B/30B/70B) across 3 storage tiers (local nvme, network fs, s3-sidecar).
- End-to-end: simulate cold-start burst (100 concurrent cold requests) to evaluate token-1 tail latency and prefetch effectiveness.
- Fault injection: corrupt chunk tests to validate quarantine detection and fallback behavior.
- Kernel scheduling interplay: A/B test with scheduler hinting on/off to measure token latency and IO savings.

Operational considerations:
- Hard limits on quarantine disk usage per node; eviction policy for old staged assets.
- Backpressure to placement/orchestration: if prefetch saturates node IO, signal autoscaler for temporary burst nodes.
- Security: all shard streams validated against manifest checksums; optional signing for enterprise/regulatory customers.

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to best derive "kernel_hint" weights from generic operator traces (per-layer vs per-kernel granularity)? Action: Marco to prototype a kernel hint encoder from perf traces. (JIRA:SRV-1292)
- Should we instrument per-page hardware-access counters (if available) or rely purely on software-level hits? Pros/cons outlined in notes.
- Policy for multi-tenant nodes: do we allow cross-session prefetching that might benefit other tenants? Default to tenant-isolation with opt-in cluster policy.
- Potential complexity: atomic activation will introduce brief manifest propagation delay — need to verify client resolvers handle transient mismatch gracefully.

Immediate next steps:
- Prototype probe-loader (PoC in rust) that performs single-page probes and exposes metrics (owner: Priya).
- Add kernel-hint proto to scheduler; implement a simple hint generator in the fusion/kernels tracer (owner: Elena).
- Design quarantine filesystem layout and checksum index format (owner: Samir).

Notes / references:
- Related experiments: see GH PR 842 for prior prefetch heuristics.
- Existing docs: weight-residency-controller-and-async-load-playbook (for eviction lifecycle) — this doc builds a more fine-grained probe/prefetch layer on top.
